Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "ridge street community greenhouse has three connected houses, and the watering rota is put on the noticeboard by the potting door. the north house is used for propagation, the middle one for potting and storage, and the south house holds the larger growing beds. on thursday 14 may, the north propagation benches were due to be watered at 6:40 in the morning. the work was done, but it did not begin until 7:18, which is 38 minutes later than the time written on the rota. it was a definite delay on that line, not a change to the whole morning's schedule. the south beds were watered on time, and nobody moved their listed time to make room for the north house.

there are six people on the rota for that week, with different jobs written beside their names so the person starting a line is not also expected to check every piece of equipment. amina was assigned to water the north propagation benches on thursday. joel was named as the back-up if she could not get to the site, though he was there that morning and did not take over her job. tessa was doing the record sheet, and marek, the maintenance technician, was available for equipment problems. omar was assigned to the south beds. their names were in the same order as the work times, but that was just how the sheet had been laid out, not a ranking of who had responsibility for the delay.

at 6:39 am, amina looked at the gauge on the north-house manifold and saw that the needle was below the green mark. when she opened the line, the water came through weakly. the trays on benches N1 to N4 were in place, and she left them where they were rather than carrying them to another part of the house. she called marek over to look at the line. the other houses were not having the same pressure problem, and omar continued with his scheduled watering in the south house. tessa noted the time and the gauge reading on the sheet. amina did not start the watering at the listed time because the flow was too low for the line to work as intended.

marek checked the manifold and the filter before he changed anything else. the valve had not been shut, the timer was working, and the header tank was about half full. he removed the filter screen and found it packed with bark fibers and potting mix. after he cleaned the screen and put it back, the pressure returned to the green range. then amina opened the north line again and began watering at 7:18. the blocked filter was the practical cause of the delay. marek said the fibers were probably left from potting work on tuesday, but he had not seen them enter the filter, so that part was his guess and not something they could confirm from the morning check.

amina later said, “I was relieved when Marek found the screen, because the timer and valve were not the problem, but I’m not sure a weekly rinse will catch this every time.” her relief was about finding a cause they could fix that morning. her doubt was about whether the proposed rinse interval would be enough on future weeks; she was not saying that the filter had failed again or that the watering had been missed altogether. the line was watered that morning after the cleaning. she also said the gauge was easy to read from the path, which made it possible to notice the weak flow before she had gone along the full length of the benches.

in the record sheet, tessa entered the scheduled time as 6:40 and the actual start as 7:18. she wrote “filter screen blocked” in the notes column and added that marek had cleaned it. she did not write that the fibers definitely came from tuesday's potting work. for the south house, the sheet shows the usual start time, with no adjustment. the record has one line for the observed pressure and another for the repair, so a later reader can see what amina noticed and what marek did without treating those as the same action. the north-house watering was recorded as completed after the delay.

there had been a short filter check written on the maintenance card before this week, but the card did not specify how often the screen should be rinsed. it lists the north manifold, the south-house branch and the header tank as separate places to inspect. marek used the small basin kept under the middle-house sink to catch the water when he took out the screen; the basin was returned there after the repair. the screen itself was not replaced, because marek said it was intact once the fibers and mix had been removed. no one reported a leak around the manifold, and the pressure gauge stayed in the green range when they checked it again after watering had started.

1. thursday notes

tessa's sheet also identifies the bench labels, N1 through N4, and records that the trays stayed in their assigned positions during the delay. the next entry on the rota is for friday's early check of the south-house beds, with omar's name beside it. a small label beside the north manifold says “filter access,” and the maintenance card is kept in the clear sleeve attached to the noticeboard. the event in the rota is therefore recorded with its own time, equipment finding and repair, while the other scheduled watering entries remain as they were.", "output": "Ridge Street Community Greenhouse has three connected houses, and the watering rota is posted by the potting-room door. The delay affected that line, not the whole morning’s schedule. The south beds were watered on time, and no one changed their listed time to accommodate the north house.

Six people were listed on that week’s rota, with different jobs beside their names so that the person starting a line was not also expected to check every piece of equipment. Amina was assigned to water the north propagation benches on Thursday. Joel was named as her back-up if she could not get to the site, but he was there that morning and did not take over her job. Tessa was completing the record sheet, and Marek, the maintenance technician, was available for equipment problems. Omar was assigned to the south beds. Their names appeared in the same order as the work times, but that was simply how the sheet was laid out, not a ranking of responsibility for the delay.

At 6:39 a.m., Amina looked at the gauge on the north-house manifold and saw that the needle was below the green mark. When she opened the line, the water flow was weak. The trays on benches N1 to N4 were in place, and she left them there rather than carrying them to another part of the house. She called Marek over to inspect the line. The other houses did not have the same pressure problem, and Omar continued his scheduled watering in the south house. Tessa noted the time and gauge reading on the sheet. Amina did not start watering at the listed time because the flow was too weak for the line to work as intended.

Marek checked the manifold and filter before changing anything else. The valve was open, the timer was working, and the header tank was about half full. He removed the filter screen and found it packed with bark fibers and potting mix. After cleaning and replacing the screen, the pressure returned to the green range. Amina then opened the north line again and began watering at 7:18. The blocked filter was the practical cause of the delay. Marek said the fibers were probably left over from potting work on Tuesday, but he had not seen them enter the filter. That part was his guess, not something they could confirm from the morning’s inspection.

Amina later said, “I was relieved when Marek found the screen, because the timer and valve were not the problem, but I’m not sure a weekly rinse will catch this every time.” Her relief was about finding a cause they could address that morning. Her doubt concerned whether the proposed rinse interval would be enough in future weeks; she was not saying that the filter had failed again or that the watering had been missed altogether. The line was watered that morning after the cleaning. She also said the gauge was easy to read from the path, making it possible to notice the weak flow before she had walked the full length of the benches.

In the record sheet, Tessa entered 6:40 as the scheduled time and 7:18 as the actual start. She wrote “filter screen blocked” in the notes column and added that Marek had cleaned it. She did not state that the fibers definitely came from Tuesday’s potting work. For the south house, the sheet shows the usual start time, with no adjustment. It has one line for the observed pressure and another for the repair, so a later reader can distinguish what Amina noticed from what Marek did. The north-house watering was recorded as completed after the delay.

A brief filter check was written on the maintenance card before this week, but the card did not specify how often the screen should be rinsed. It lists the north manifold, the south-house branch, and the header tank as separate places to inspect. Marek used the small basin kept under the middle-house sink to catch water when he removed the screen; the basin was returned there after the repair. The screen was not replaced because Marek said it was intact once the fibers and potting mix had been removed. No one reported a leak around the manifold, and the pressure gauge remained in the green range when they checked it again after watering had started.

1. Thursday notes

Tessa’s sheet also identifies the bench labels, N1 through N4, and records that the trays stayed in their assigned positions during the delay. The next entry on the rota is for Friday’s early check of the south-house beds, with Omar’s name beside it. A small label beside the north manifold says “filter access,” and the maintenance card is kept in the clear sleeve attached to the noticeboard. The rota entry records the event with its own time, equipment finding, and repair, while the other scheduled watering entries remain unchanged."}]
